main_topics.reason: The user came to understand which RA treatments could fit with trying for a baby and returned to planning a safe transition.
The user asked whether being on methotrexate now was concerning and recognized the need for contraception while taking it.
The user asked what options would remain if a pregnancy-compatible medication did not control RA as well.
The user asked whether RA changes during pregnancy and followed up about postpartum flares.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medications could also be used while breastfeeding.
The user asked whom to coordinate with and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now.
The user described fear of having to choose between their health and having a baby, then said the conversation eased that anxiety.

output.summary: Recently diagnosed with RA, the user hopes to try for a baby in one to two years and asked about medication choices, methotrexate safety, timing a switch, disease control, pregnancy and postpartum changes, and breastfeeding. The assistant discussed compatible treatment options and care coordination; the user said the plan was clear, intended to raise it at the next rheumatology visit, and felt less anxious and more in control.
